introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Container runtime security in production relies on hand-written rules (Falco, Tetragon), which miss behaviour nobody anticipated; syscall anomaly detection could cover that gap but must be fast, cheap and quiet enough to run on a live cluster.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Most syscall anomaly detectors are evaluated offline on recorded traces with labels used for tuning; few measure kernel-to-responder latency, alert burden on a real workload, or the confusion between attacks and harmless new processes (operator kubectl exec). Scope: one cluster with one 21-workload application, LID-DS 2021 and CB-DS.
search_directions: Foundational sequence-based syscall anomaly detection (Forrest et al. 1996 'A sense of self for Unix processes'; Warrender et al. 1999)
Surveys or SoK of host-based intrusion detection with system calls and of pitfalls in ML for security (Arp et al. 'Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security')
Container and Kubernetes runtime security monitoring with eBPF in practice (Falco, Tetragon, Tracee comparisons)
Language-model approaches to system call sequences (Kim et al. 2016 LSTM-based system call language modeling)

related_work_strategy.overview: Three clusters that precede or compete with the design, each with the limitation the paper addresses.

content_bullets: Problem: rule-based runtime security misses unknown behaviour; syscall anomaly detection rarely measured live.
Method: in-kernel return-value tokens, per-thread 4-gram counts, per-workload count language model, normal-only Gumbel threshold, one-window alarm, push to Alertmanager.

Results: LID-DS 2021 official 97.40 % recall at 0.33 % false-alarm recordings, p95 1.47 s; CB-DS 891/891; blind live 314/314 primary attacks, 0/314 control, kernel->Alertmanager p95 0.68 s; overhead 0.4-0.5 us per simple syscall.
Honest limits: flags harmless new processes; blind to seen-only attackers; lineage separation as the next step (v6 results when available). <= 200 words.
Hook and gap per introduction_strategy.
Three measured requirements: latency to the responder, burden on a real workload, separation from benign new processes.
Contributions list (idea.md 'Contributions'), each with its headline number from experimental_log.md E1, E3, E5, E4/E7.
Pre-registration and development/blind split stated up front.
